validated_results.title: Dairy products, calcium, and prostate cancer risk in the Physicians' Health Study.
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of US physicians reporting dairy calcium intake and incident prostate cancer with a target-specific relative risk.

extraction.comparison_type: >600 mg Ca/d from dairy products vs <=150 mg Ca/d from dairy products

sample_size.excerpt: During 11 y of follow-up, we documented 1012 incident cases of prostate cancer among 20885 men.

cases.excerpt: During 11 y of follow-up, we documented 1012 incident cases of prostate cancer among 20885 men.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with men consuming < or =0.5 daily servings of dairy products, those consuming >2.5 servings had a multivariate relative risk of prostate cancer of 1.34 (95% CI: 1.04, 1.71) after adjustment for baseline age, body mass index, smoking, exercise, and randomized treatment assignment in the original placebo-controlled trial. Compared with men consuming < or =150 mg Ca/d from dairy products, men consuming >600 mg/d had a 32% higher risk of prostate cancer (95% CI: 1.08, 1.63).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with men consuming < or =150 mg Ca/d from dairy products, men consuming >600 mg/d had a 32% higher risk of prostate cancer (95% CI: 1.08, 1.63).
